text: 1 % Part b - randomly generate sequence 2 P = [0.8 0.2 0.0; 3 0.4 0.4 0.2; 4 0.2 0.6 0.2]; 5 6 seq = simulate_weather(P, 50, 1); % start from Sunny, simulate 50 steps 7 % Map 1/2/3 to 'S','C','R' if you want: 8 labels = 'SCR'; 9 disp(labels(seq)); 10 11 % Part c - estimate stationary distribution using long run frequencies 12 Nburn = 5000; % burn-in 13 Nkeep = 1000000; % sample size after burn-in 14 15 traj = simulate_weather(P, Nburn + Nkeep, 1); % start anywhere (1=S here) 16 traj = traj(Nburn+l:end); 17 18 % empirical frequencies 19 p_hat = [mean(traj==1), mean(traj==2), mean(traj==3)]; 20 fprintf('Estimated stationary (S,C,R) = (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n', p_hat); 21 22 % simulate_weather function 23 function states = simulate_weather(P, N, init) 24 % generate a sequence of weather states from a Markov chain. 25 % P is 3x3 transition matrix (rows sum to 1) in order [S C R]. 26 % N is number of days to simulate. 27 % init is initial state index: 1=Sunny, 2=Cloudy, 3=Rainy._ 28 % returns: states(1:N) as indices 1=S, 2=C, 3=R. 29 30 assert(all(abs(sum(P,2)-1) < 1le-12), 'Rows of P must sum to 1'); 31 states = zeros(1,N); 32 states(1l) = init; 33 34 for t = 2:N 35 row = P(states(t-1), :); 36 u = rand; % uniform(@,1) 37 c = cumsum(row); 38 states(t) = find(u <= ¢, 1); % inverse-CDF sampling 39 end 40 end Command Window >> A3Q1 SSSCSSSSSCSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSCRRCCSCCSSSSSCCSSSSCCRC Estimated stationary (S,C,R) = (0.6424, 0.2860, 0.0716)
